evals.name: routing-triggers
evals.prompt: set up the /test-app skill for this repo
evals.expected_output: test-app-create loads, detects the stack, and writes a tailored .claude/skills/test-app/SKILL.md plus its references/subagent-prompt.md.

evals.name: routing-excludes-test-app
evals.prompt: test the app and check the checkout flow still works
evals.expected_output: Actually exercising the running app is the generated test-app skill's job; test-app-create must not load, because it generates that skill rather than running it.

evals.name: routing-triggers-tui
evals.prompt: scaffold /test-app for this ratatui app so i can smoke-test the pane changes
evals.expected_output: test-app-create loads, Step 0 resolves the surface to tui, and it writes the PROCESS template pair — the generated skill drives a real terminal and never mentions a base URL or /agent-browser.

evals.name: routing-triggers-cli
evals.prompt: i've got a cobra cli here, make me a test skill for this repo
evals.expected_output: test-app-create loads and resolves the surface to cli — the generated skill asserts exit codes and stdout/stderr separation against the built binary, and there is no visual pass.

evals.name: routing-excludes-run
evals.prompt: start the TUI so I can see the new filter pane working
evals.expected_output: Launching the app to look at it is /run's job. test-app-create must not load: it GENERATES the skill that tests an app, and generating one here would be a large unasked-for write in place of a one-line launch.

evals.name: surface-discriminator
evals.prompt: scaffold the test-app skill for this project
evals.expected_output: Resolves the surface to cli, NOT tui. The fixture carries ratatui in [dev-dependencies] only, clap in [dependencies], and no alternate-screen call anywhere — so a dependency-name match says tui and the discriminator must overrule it. This is the hardest input Step 0 gets: a wrong answer here picks the wrong template pair for the whole generated skill, and every check in it then asks the wrong questions of the right program.
